{"type": "content", "content": "The full pipeline ran and `report/report.md` is finished, with 12 figures, 5 tables and all code in `code/`. Everything is in silico: no synthesis or MD was possible. The model that scores the designs (an MD-trained surrogate plus calibration) was trained on the same 8,424 MD values as the generator, so its "hits" show the two models agree. They are not independent validation.

**Calibrating MD Tg against experiment**
- Raw MD over-predicts Tg by about 64 K on average (error 70.6 K). The Gaussian-process correction brings the leave-one-out error down to **16.3 K** (18.1 K under strict 5-fold refitting), with well-calibrated uncertainty.
- On the six real epoxy/phenoxy resins, held out as a whole family, the error is **16.2 K** against 56.7 K for raw MD.
- Applied to the 8,424 vitrimers, it lowers Tg by 51 K on average, in line with the bias above. Uncertainty stays around ±33 K because vitrimers are about 4× larger than any calibration polymer and chemically quite different.

**Generative model** (separate acid and epoxide encoders and decoders, plus a Tg predictor)
- 82–92 % of molecules generated even from random points are correctly functionalised (exactly two COOH, or exactly two terminal epoxides).
- The weak spot is exact reconstruction of training molecules, at 3–6 %. The decoder also starts overfitting after about 20 epochs.
- β = 0.1 gave the best balance in a comparison of three settings.

**Chemistry space and Bayesian optimisation**
- All 15.4k monomers were encoded once, giving a screen of 10⁶ new acid×epoxide pairs. The fast predictor has 6.6 K error on held-out pairs and matches the scoring model at r = 0.95.
- Optimisation produced 1,522 new valid designs over four goals. Hit rates within ±5 K were 30 % at 373 K and 17 % at 300 K, against 16 % and 0.3 % in the library.
- It reached slightly past the library range: **498.5 ± 35 K** above the 486 K maximum, and **247.8 ± 31 K** below the 263 K minimum.
- Three caveats on those results:
  - The margins (+12 / −15 K) are smaller than the uncertainty.
  - On the raw MD scale the best high-Tg designs do *not* beat the library; the gain comes entirely from the structure-dependent correction.
  - Optimisation clearly beat a random-search control only for maximum Tg and the 373 K target. Simply recombining existing monomers in the 10⁶ screen did as well or better at both extremes.
- The top high-Tg design has an implausible eight-membered ring, so a synthesizability filter is needed before choosing anything to make.

**Validation evidence**
